title: Motion
seo_title: Motion Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Motion: Distance and displacement, velocity; uniform and non-uniform motion along a straight line; acceleration, distance-time and velocity-time graphs for uniform motion and uniformly accelerated motion, elementary idea of uniform circular motion.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7: distance and displacement, speed and velocity, km/h and m/s, acceleration, the three equations of motion, graphs and uniform circular motion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² − u² = 2as.
key_sub: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish.
body_html:
How to think about it

Distance is the total path length; displacement is the shortest distance from the start to the finish in a given direction, so it can be zero. Speed is distance ÷ time; velocity is speed in a given direction. To change km/h into m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Acceleration is the change in velocity per second: a = (v − u) ÷ t. For uniform acceleration the equations of motion are v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² and v² − u² = 2as. On a velocity–time graph the slope is the acceleration and the area under the line is the displacement. Uniform circular motion is accelerated because the direction keeps changing.

Example

72 km/h in m/s?

72 × 5/18

Answer: 20 m/s

Example

u = 0, a = 2 m/s², t = 5 s. Distance?

s = ½ × 2 × 25

Answer: 25 m

Common mistakes

  • Taking the average of two speeds as the average speed.
  • Forgetting that a returning object has zero displacement.
  • Using km/h and seconds in the same equation.

faq.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
faq.a: Speed has only size; velocity is speed in a given direction, so it can change when only the direction changes.

faq.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph show?
faq.a: The displacement (distance travelled) in that time.

items.q: A truck from Delhi covers 90 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 90 ÷ 2 = 45 km/h.

items.q: Pooja walks 60 m east and then 80 m north. What is the magnitude of the displacement?
items.e: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish: √(60² + 80²) = 100 m; the distance walked is 140 m.

items.q: A train from Delhi covers 250 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 250 ÷ 5 = 50 km/h.

A train from Delhi covers 200 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 km/h.

items.q: What does a straight line sloping upwards on a distance–time graph show?
items.e: Equal distances are covered in equal times.

items.q: Can the displacement of an object be zero while the distance is not?

items.e: A full lap of a track has zero displacement.

items.q: What does the slope of a velocity–time graph give?
items.e: A horizontal line means zero acceleration.

items.q: Why do we need a reference point to describe motion?

items.e: A passenger is at rest relative to the bus but moving relative to the road.
